Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1962 reads `terreno` where 1862 reads `terrcmo`; 1962 reads `gloriam` where 1862 reads `gl6riam`; 1962 has nothing there; 1862 has `:`; 1962 reads `precibus` where 1862 reads `pr6eibus`; 1962 reads `Dominum.` where 1862 reads `D6minum.`; 1862 capitalises Martyrii where the 1962 does not; 1862 spells coelestem where the 1962 spells caelestem: orthography; 1862 sets a comma where the 1962 sets a semicolon before the last clause; 1862 prints the j-orthography (ejus, ejusdem); 1862 layer damages two words (terrcmo for terreno, pr6eibus for precibus); both are unambiguous and both are clean in the 1962 and in the 1922 Mame at 28 September; 1862 conclusion is the short cue and so is the 1962's here. Corroboration: 1922 Mame carries 28 September in its universal sanctoral (PDF p. 839); not transcribed, the 1862 settles the reading.
